claims.text: Removing Co from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi alters the alloy's stacking-fault energy.
Co removal produces a sharper temperature- and strain-rate-dependent transition between dislocation glide and deformation twinning.
The altered glide-to-twinning transition tunes the strength–ductility balance of Co-free FeNiCrMn.
The Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy has a solidified, single-phase, equiatomic solid-solution microstructure.
Mechanical testing from cryogenic to room temperature and from quasi-static to high strain rates can reveal the proposed mechanism transition.
Stacking-fault energy is especially temperature-sensitive in the proposed low-to-moderate temperature range.
Deformation-induced twin boundaries and evolving dislocation structures mediate the mechanical response.
Twin nucleation is governed by stacking-fault energy.
Removing Co enhances the sensitivity of stacking-fault energy to temperature and strain rate.
Conditions producing lower stacking-fault energy activate deformation twinning.
Deformation twinning supplies additional plasticity and work hardening.
When twinning is suppressed, dislocation glide dominates and produces higher strength.
Relative to CoCrFeMnNi, Co-free FeNiCrMn will show reduced twin density and higher strength at lower temperatures or higher strain rates.
Relative to CoCrFeMnNi, Co-free FeNiCrMn will show increased twinning, ductility, and work hardening at higher temperatures or lower strain rates.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi is an appropriate Co-containing baseline alloy.
CoCrFeMnNi has a more gradual or less condition-sensitive deformation-mechanism shift than Co-free FeNiCrMn.
The proposed mechanism may cease to apply when phase decomposition or other microstructural instabilities occur.
Parallel tests under identical conditions, with microscopy and mechanical measurements, provide a controlled comparison between the Co-free and Co-containing alloys.
The hypothesis is falsified if the Co-free alloy shows no statistically significant condition-dependent difference in twin density or mechanical response relative to CoCrFeMnNi.
